gloss: kneeling on the ground (in apology or supplication)

definitions.gloss: kneeling on the ground; prostrating oneself
definitions.explanation: The act of kneeling on the ground and pressing one's forehead to the floor as an extreme gesture of apology, gratitude, or supplication. One of the most dramatic forms of showing deference in Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{土下座|どげざ}して{謝|あやま}った。
examples.english: He prostrated himself on the ground and apologized.

examples.japanese: {土下座|どげざ}されても{許|ゆる}せない。
examples.english: I can't forgive them even if they prostrate themselves.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}が{記者会見|きしゃかいけん}で{土下座|どげざ}する{姿|すがた}がニュースになった。
examples.english: The sight of the company president prostrating himself at the press conference became news.

notes:
USAGE:
Performed by dropping to the knees and pressing the forehead to the ground with hands flat on the floor. It represents the most extreme form of apology or plea in Japanese culture. In modern usage, it sometimes appears in exaggerated or humorous contexts as well.

The verb form is {土下座|どげざ}する.

CULTURE:
Historically, {土下座|どげざ} was performed before feudal lords and officials as a sign of absolute submission. In modern Japan, it is reserved for the most serious apologies or desperate pleas. Forcing someone to perform {土下座|どげざ} can constitute a criminal offense ({強要罪|きょうようざい}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {土下座|どげざ}して{謝|あやま}る (to prostrate and apologize)
- {土下座|どげざ}して{頼|たの}む (to prostrate and beg)
- {土下座|どげざ}を{強要|きょうよう}する (to force someone to prostrate)
